children.translated_text: Endowed with naturally meritorious and worthy virtues, and gathered from the words of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One),

children.text: śubhamālakṣya kṛtā vai kāścidāryāgītayastvayā ca śravyāḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: having observed what is auspicious, I have indeed composed some noble songs that should be heard by you. (Verse 1)

children.text: dārumayī hyapi pratimā sampūjyate kāpi sugatasya vidvadbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even a wooden image of the <s>Sugata</s> is worshipped by the wise;

children.text: tathāmanojñaṃ kāvyaṃ saddharmāśrayācca mamedaṃ na nindyam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: likewise, though this poem of mine is not elegant, being grounded in the true <s>Dharma</s>, it should not be disparaged. (Verse 2)
The exceedingly sweet words of the great Sage, I believe, must already be known to you;

children.text: ākalpitaṃ tu sudhayā nanvatidhavalaṃ na dṛśyate candrikayā? || 3 ||
children.translated_text: but when coated with plaster, is not the moonlight seen to be even more brilliantly white? (Verse 3)
The six <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections) — of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṅgha</s>, <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>tyāga</s> (generosity), and the <s>devas</s> (gods) —
have been set forth by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors); they should be recollected individually through their respective collections of qualities. (Verse 4)
The ten wholesome courses of action should always be practiced through body, speech, and mind;
having refrained from intoxicants and the like, and with a pure livelihood consisting of meritorious deeds, you should be well-pleased. (Verse 5)
Knowing wealth to be unstable and without essence, gifts should be given properly to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, mendicants, the poor, and friends;

children.text: dānaṃ deyaṃ vidhinā janmāntareṣu na dānāt paraṃ mitram || 6 ||
children.translated_text: in future lives, there is no friend greater than generosity. (Verse 6)
<s>Śīla</s> (moral conduct) should be observed by you — unmixed, unimpaired, untransgressed, and unstained;

children.text: carācarapratiṣṭhaṃ tu guṇāśrayaṃ bhūvacca rājate śīlam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: the foundation of all moving and unmoving things, the basis of virtues — <s>śīla</s> shines like the earth. (Verse 7)
These six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) — <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (conduct), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (effort), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) —
having cultivated them immeasurably, one becomes a <s>Jinendra</s> (Lord of Victors), having crossed to the far shore of the ocean of existence. (Verse 8)

children.text: yatra pūjā pitṝṇāṃ kulaṃ tadācāryabrahmabhiḥ samṛddham /
children.translated_text: Where there is worship of parents, that family, enriched by teachers and <s>Brahmā</s>,
through that worship, fame [is obtained], and thereafter higher rebirth (<s>abhyudaya</s>) is also attained. (Verse 9)
Violence, theft, intoxication, sexual misconduct, lying, singing, and dancing
should be abandoned, as should eating at improper times, garlands, perfumes, and other luxuries, and high beds. (Verse 10)
If one observes the <s>upoṣadha</s> (observance day) with the eight components, emulating the conduct of the <s>Arhats</s>,

children.text: labhate hi pumān strī vā suramyakāmāvacarādidevakāyam || 11 ||
children.translated_text: a man or woman obtains [rebirth in] the lovely <s>Kāmāvacara</s> (sense-realm) divine bodies and higher. (Verse 11)
Envy, deceit, guile, pride, attachment, laziness, desire, and hatred —
the intoxication born from family, beauty, youth, learning, strength, and so forth — regard these as enemies. (Verse 12)
'Heedfulness is the abode of the deathless; heedlessness is the abode of death' — thus the Sage has taught;
for the increase of wholesome qualities, heedfulness should always be practiced by you. (Verse 13)
Whoever was formerly heedless and afterward becomes heedful, like the moon emerging from clouds —
he shines beautifully, comparable to <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Aṅgulimāla</s>, <s>Udayana</s>, and <s>Ajātaśatru</s>. (Verse 14)

children.text: kṣāntisamaṃ naiva tapastatastvayā na krodhāvasaro deyaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no austerity equal to patience; therefore no occasion should be given to anger by you;
the <s>Buddha</s> has indeed declared that the stage of non-regression is attained through the abandonment of anger. (Verse 15)
'He reviled me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me of my wealth' —

children.text: vairairebhiḥ kalahastyajati ya etad vairaṃ sa sukhaṃ śete || 16 ||
children.translated_text: whoever abandons this enmity through these hostilities, sleeps happily. (Verse 16)

children.text: jale 'vanau pāṣāṇe citramiva cittaṃ tridhā khalu sattvānām /
children.translated_text: The mind of beings is threefold — like [writing on] water, earth, and stone;
the first belongs to those who have afflictions; the last, belonging to those who desire the <s>Dharma</s>, is the best. (Verse 17)
Speech is declared by the <s>Jina</s> to be threefold among people — sweet, true, and false;
these are respectively like honey, flowers, and filth; and the last is to be abandoned. (Verse 18)

children.text: caturvidhā vai puruṣāḥ prakāśātprakāśe tamasastamasi punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Persons are of four kinds: from light to light, from darkness to darkness,

children.text: tamaḥ prakāśād gacchati tamasastejasi pudgalo varaḥ prathamaḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: going from darkness to light, and from light to darkness — the person who goes from darkness to light is the best, the first. (Verse 19)
Like a mango fruit — ripe though appearing unripe, unripe though appearing ripe,

children.text: apakve 'pakvaṃ tathā pakve pakvamiva bhāti cāturvidhyam || 20 ||
children.translated_text: unripe and appearing unripe, and ripe and appearing ripe — such is the fourfold [classification] that appears among people. (Verse 20)

children.text: paradārānna tu paśyed dṛṣṭe ca jñeyā avasthānurūpyeṇa /
children.translated_text: One should not look at another's wife; and if seen, one should regard her according to the appropriate relationship —
as a maiden, mother, or sister; and even if attached, one should contemplate [her body as] impure. (Verse 21)
Guard the restless mind most carefully, as one guards hearing, a son, a treasure, or life;
the mind should be kept away from sense-desire, which is like an enemy, a serpent, poison, a weapon, or fire. (Verse 22)
Sense-desire has been declared by the <s>Jinendra</s> to be a producer of harm, comparable to the <s>kimpāka</s> fruit;

children.text: pāśaistasya hi baddho bhavacārake lokaḥ sa prahātavyaḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: bound by its snares, the world [wanders] in the prison of existence — it should be abandoned. (Verse 23)

children.text: calādhruvāṇi ṣaḍakṣāṇi jayanti samare vā śatrūnapi caike /
children.translated_text: The six unsteady, unreliable senses — some conquer even enemies in battle;

children.text: tayośca sudhiyaḥ prathamaṃ varamindriyavijetāraṃ ca manyante || 24 ||
children.translated_text: between those two, the wise consider the first — the conqueror of the senses — to be the better. (Verse 24)
The body of a young woman is foul; it is a vessel of impurity with nine doors of impurity;
covered with skin, insatiable — even when adorned with ornaments, it should be viewed separately [from its ornaments]. (Verse 25)

children.text: kṛmipīḍito hi kuṣṭhī sukhalipsayā ca yathā vahnimāśrayate /
children.translated_text: Just as a leper afflicted by worms takes refuge in fire out of desire for comfort,

children.text: pīḍā na yāti śāntiṃ tathaiva hi kāmāsaktirapi boddhavyā || 26 ||
children.translated_text: yet the affliction does not find relief — so too attachment to sense-desires should be understood. (Verse 26)

children.text: paramārthaṃ prativettuṃ sarvabhāveṣu savidhi manasi nidhāyaiva /
children.translated_text: In order to understand the ultimate truth, having properly placed [it] in the mind regarding all phenomena,

children.text: sa ca khalu bhāvayitavyo na hi tattulyo 'paro guṇayuto dharmaḥ || 27 ||
children.translated_text: that indeed should be cultivated; for there is no other quality-endowed <s>dharma</s> equal to that. (Verse 27)

children.text: sukulīno 'pi na pūjyo jñānaśīlavimukho śrutirūpavān pumān /
children.translated_text: Even a man of good family who is devoid of knowledge and moral conduct is not worthy of worship, though he may possess learning and beauty;
one endowed with those two qualities is always worthy of worship, even if lacking in other qualities. (Verse 28)
Regarding the eight worldly <s>dharmas</s>, one who knows the world should maintain the mind in equanimity —
in loss and gain, fame and disgrace, praise and blame, happiness and suffering — [all of which are] not to be grieved over. (Verse 29)
By you, toward <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, monks, gods, guests, mothers, fathers, families, and chief queens,

children.text: pāpaṃ nācaraṇiyaṃ yataḥ katamo 'pi na narakaphalasya bhāgī || 30 ||
children.translated_text: no evil should be committed, since anyone [who does so] becomes a sharer in the fruit of hell. (Verse 30)

children.text: na ca kṛntati pāpakarma tatkṣaṇamastrapātavat kamapi pāpinam /
children.translated_text: Evil <s>karma</s> does not cut the evildoer immediately like a weapon's blow;
but at the time of death, the fruit of that action surely presents itself. (Verse 31)
Seven treasures have been declared: faith, moral conduct, generosity, purity, learning, and wisdom,

children.text: apatrapā hrī muninā mudhaivāparadhanāni hi sādhāraṇāni || 32 ||
children.translated_text: modesty and conscientiousness — [these] by the Sage; other treasures are merely common. (Verse 32)
Gambling, spectacle-watching, laziness, association with bad friends, intoxicants,
and wandering at night — these six should be abandoned, as they bestow evil destinies and destroy reputation. (Verse 33)
By the lord of men, gods, and sages, contentment has been declared the foremost of all wealth;

children.text: santoṣo 'nuṣṭheyaḥ dhanaṃ vinaiva sa dhanikaḥ sati santoṣe || 34 ||
children.translated_text: contentment should be practiced; for one who has contentment is wealthy even without wealth. (Verse 34)

children.text: yathā samṛddhāḥ puruṣā duḥkhino bhavanti naiva tathālpecchukāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as wealthy men suffer, those of few desires do not suffer in the same way;

children.text: yāvatyaḥ santi phaṇā ārya, duḥkhakarāḥ, nāgasya tāvatyaḥ || 35 ||
children.translated_text: O noble one, as many hoods as the serpent has, so many are its causes of suffering. (Verse 35)

children.text: patnī tyājyā trividhā prakṛtyā ripusambaddhā svaghātikeva /
children.translated_text: A wife of three types should be abandoned — one who is by nature like an enemy or connected to enemies, like a murderess;
one who dishonors her husband, who is wanton, who delights in stealing petty things — like a thief. (Verse 36)
One who is agreeable like a sister, dear to the heart like a friend, should be served;
one who is helpful like a mother should be honored; one who follows orders like a servant — like a goddess. (Verse 37)
Having abandoned attachment and aversion, one should take food as medicine, understanding [its purpose];

children.text: kāyasthityai nitarāṃ na ca saundaryagarvamānārthaṃ sevyam || 38 ||
children.translated_text: it should be taken solely for maintaining the body, not for the sake of beauty, pride, vanity, or gain. (Verse 38)

children.text: dinamakhilaṃ śubhakārye yāpayed rātrerādyantau yāmau ca /
children.translated_text: Spend the entire day in virtuous activity, and the first and last watches of the night as well;

children.text: dhīman, madhye yāme śayīta yato hi na bhaved viphalā nidrā || 39 ||
children.translated_text: O wise one, sleep during the middle watch, so that sleep is not in vain. (Verse 39)
<s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), and <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) should always be properly cultivated;
even without attaining the supreme state, one surely obtains happiness in the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (world of Brahmā). (Verse 40)

children.text: kāmān prītivicārau sukhañca duḥkhañca vihāya caturbhireva /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned sense-desires, joy, investigation, happiness, and suffering, through the four
<s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) alone, one becomes a sharer in [the heavens of] <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, and <s>Bṛhatphala</s>. (Verse 41)
Wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> always arises from five factors: persistent involvement, absence of an antidote, substance, and qualities;
therefore one should strive in the practice of wholesome conduct. (Verse 42)
Just as a little alkaline water transforms the taste of a little water but not that of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (Ganges),

children.text: pāpaṃ tathaiva cālpaṃ nāśayatyalpakuśalaṃ na pūrṇakuśalam || 43 ||
children.translated_text: so too a small amount of evil destroys a small amount of merit, but not full merit. (Verse 43)

children.text: auddhatyaṃ kaukṛtyaṃ vyāpādaḥ styānamiddhe ca kāmecchā /
children.translated_text: Restlessness, remorse, ill-will, torpor and drowsiness, sense-desire,
and doubt — these five should be known as the robbers of the treasure of wholesome qualities. (Verse 44)
The five supreme qualities are faith, effort, mindfulness, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom);
these are called the supreme powers and faculties; therefore one should strive in them. (Verse 45)
All are subject to <s>karma</s>, just as [they are subject to] sickness, old age, death, and separation from loved ones;

children.text: punaḥ punastu cintayā pratipakṣeṇaivaṃ prahīyate mānaḥ || 46 ||
children.translated_text: by repeatedly contemplating with this antidote, pride is thus abandoned. (Verse 46)
If one desires heaven and liberation, right view should first be cultivated;
even good deeds performed by persons with wrong views have terrible results. (Verse 47)
The person should be rightly known as without self, impure, suffering, and impermanent;
those who lack the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) are destroyed by the four perversions. (Verse 48)

children.text: uktaṃ rūpaṃ nātmā rūpavāṃśca nātmā rūpe naivātmā /
children.translated_text: It is said: form is not the self, nor is the possessor of form the self; in form there is no self,

children.text: na cātmanyasti rūpaṃ śūnyamevaṃ skandhacatuṣkamapi jñeyam || 49 ||
children.translated_text: nor does form exist in the self — likewise the other four <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) should be known as empty. || Sl_49 ||

children.text: skandhā na hi jāyante yadṛcchayā na prakṛtīśvarakālebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>skandhas</s> are not born by chance, nor from <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>Īśvara</s> (God), or <s>kāla</s> (time);

children.text: nāhetoḥ svabhāvato jñeyā ajñānena tṛṣṇayā jātāḥ || 50 ||
children.translated_text: nor without cause, nor from their own inherent nature — they should be known as born from <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance) and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving). || Sl_50 ||

children.text: kālaḥ pacati bhūtāni kālaḥ saṃharate prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Time ripens all beings, time gathers creatures together,

children.text: kālaḥ supteṣu jāgarti kālo hi duratikramaḥ //
children.translated_text: time wakes those who sleep — for time is indeed hard to overcome.
The false view of self, attachment to rites and rituals, and doubt —
one should understand these three fetters as obstructions to the gateway of liberation. || Sl_51 ||

children.text: ātmāpekṣo mokṣaḥ parasmānna labhyate kimapi sāhāyyam /
children.translated_text: Liberation depends on oneself; no help whatsoever is obtained from another;
one should practice the four <s>āryasatyas</s> (noble truths) through hearing and reflection while established in moral conduct. || Sl_52 ||
The three trainings — in higher morality, mind, and wisdom — should always be cultivated;
within these are included the one hundred and fifty-one training rules. || Sl_53 ||
O King, mindfulness of the body has been declared by the <s>Buddha</s> to be the one path;
guard this with effort, for from the loss of mindfulness comes the destruction of all <s>dharmas</s>. || Sl_54 ||
Life has many afflictions and is impermanent like a water-bubble blown by the wind;
it is a wonder that one wakes after a moment's sleep, still breathing in and out. || Sl_55 ||
The body is subject to disintegration and decay, is putrid, will dry up, is insubstantial, of impure nature;

children.text: rajaḥsadharmī cānte sadā viyogaśīlo naśvaro jñeyaḥ || 56 ||
children.translated_text: it shares the nature of dust, and in the end is always subject to separation — it should be known as perishable. || Sl_56 ||
The earth, <s>Meru</s>, and the oceans will not remain after the seven suns' flames;

children.text: dhūlimātraṃ hi mūrtāḥ kā kathā durbalavapuṣāṃ mānavānām || 57 ||
children.translated_text: not even dust will remain of material things — what need be said of weak-bodied humans? || Sl_57 ||
Thus everything is impermanent, without self, without refuge, without protector, without abode;
O King, like a plantain tree, withdraw your mind from this insubstantial <s>saṃsāra</s>. || Sl_58 ||
Human birth is as rare as a turtle inserting its neck through a hole in a yoke in the great ocean;
it is extremely difficult to obtain from animal birth and the like — make it fruitful through practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>, O Lord of Men. || Sl_59 ||
Some fill a golden vessel adorned with jewels with excrement;
more foolish than that is one who, having obtained human birth, still commits sin. || Sl_60 ||
Dwelling in a favorable place, reliance on good persons, and auspicious aspirations,
along with one's own prior merit — these four wheels exist in you. || Sl_61 ||
Association with a spiritual friend has been taught by the Sage for the perfection of the holy life;

children.text: sevyaḥ sadā supuruṣaḥ śamaḥ prāpto yato jinamapekṣya bahubhiḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: one should always associate with a good person — many have attained peace by relying on the <s>Jina</s>. || Sl_62 ||
One with wrong views, born in a frontier region, born among hell-beings, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), or animals,

children.text: mleccho jaḍaśca sattvo yo hyutpanno buddhavirahite || 63 ||
children.translated_text: a barbarian, a dull being, or one born when a <s>Buddha</s> is absent — || Sl_63 ||
one born in the long-lived god-realm — these eight unfavorable conditions are defects;

children.text: ebhī rahito bhūtvā kṣaṇaṃ labdhvā janmanivṛttau prayateta || 64 ||
children.translated_text: having become free from them and obtained the favorable moment, one should strive for the cessation of birth. || Sl_64 ||
<s>Saṃsāra</s> brings suffering such as the destruction of what is desired, disease, death, old age, and the like;

children.text: virajya tataḥ śṛṇu tāvad doṣānetasyāvagacchan naradeva || 65 ||
children.translated_text: becoming disenchanted with it, hear now the defects of this, and understand them, O Lord of Men. || Sl_65 ||

children.text: mitratvena ca śatruḥ putratvena pitāmbā ca bhāryātvena /
children.translated_text: An enemy becomes a friend, a father becomes a son, a mother becomes a wife;
they are born in reversed roles — therefore nothing is fixed in this <s>saṃsāra</s>. || Sl_66 ||
More breast-milk of mothers has been drunk by people than the water of the four oceans;
following the way of ordinary beings, the world will drink still more than that. || Sl_67 ||
A heap of one's own bones would grow as high as or higher than <s>Meru</s>;
the earth's clay could not count, even in pellets the size of berries, one's mothers. || Sl_68 ||

children.text: lokapūjyo 'pi śakraḥ patati ca punaḥ karmavaśāddhi saṃsāre /
children.translated_text: Even <s>Śakra</s>, worshipped by the world, falls again by the force of <s>karma</s> in <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: tadvacca cakravartī rājāpi punarbhavati hi dāso loke || 69 ||
children.translated_text: likewise even a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) king becomes a servant in the world again. || Sl_69 ||
Having long enjoyed the pleasure born from touching the breasts of celestial nymphs in heaven,
one endures unbearable suffering in hell from crushing, cutting, splitting, and machines. || Sl_70 ||
Having long enjoyed the pleasure of walking on the blissful summit of <s>Meru</s>, where the feet touch softly,
one should always reflect in mind on the intense suffering of hot ashes and putrid corpses. || Sl_71 ||

children.text: devāṅganāsevite nandane ramye copavane ca vihṛtya /
children.translated_text: Having sported in the lovely <s>Nandana</s> grove attended by divine maidens,
their hands, feet, ears, and noses are cut off in the <s>Asipattravana</s> (Sword-leaf Forest). || Sl_72 ||
Having bathed in the <s>Mandākinī</s> river with beautiful god-daughters adorned with golden lotuses,

children.text: snātvā punaśca narake kṣāroṣṇodakavaitaraṇyāṃ hi patanti || 73 ||
children.translated_text: they fall again into the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> river of hell with its caustic, boiling water. || Sl_73 ||
Having attained the happiness of desire among the gods and the happiness of desirelessness in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>,
one constantly obtains suffering in <s>Avīci</s>, becoming fuel for the fire. || Sl_74 ||

children.text: padamavāpya suryendvoḥ svakāyaprabhayā pradīpya hi saṃsāram /
children.translated_text: Having attained the position of Sun and Moon, illuminating <s>saṃsāra</s> with the radiance of one's own body,

children.text: tamasi ca ghane praviṣṭaḥ prasāritamapi ca svīyakaraṃ na paśyati || 75 ||
children.translated_text: having entered thick darkness, one cannot see even one's own outstretched hand. || Sl_75 ||
Thus, knowing death, the light of the lamp of threefold merit should be grasped;
otherwise one must enter into a darkness that cannot be dispelled by the Sun or Moon. || Sl_76 ||
Beings attached to evil conduct suffer constantly in the <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, and <s>Tapana</s> hells,

children.text: rauravāvīcyādau hi saṃghāte cāpi narake sadā duḥkham || 77 ||
children.translated_text: in <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, and also in the <s>Saṃghāta</s> hell. || Sl_77 ||

children.text: niṣpīḍyante tilavat kecanānye cūrṇavat peṣyante ca /
children.translated_text: Some are crushed like sesame seeds, others are ground to powder;
some are cut with saws, and likewise split with sharp axes. || Sl_78 ||
Into the mouths of others, blazing molten iron is poured;

children.text: āropyante kecana sakaṇṭake taptāyase sadā śūle || 79 ||
children.translated_text: some are constantly impaled on sharp, heated iron stakes. || Sl_79 ||
Some are torn apart by fierce dogs with iron teeth, roaring;

children.text: utthāya karau vivaśā luñcyante tīkṣṇanakhatuṇḍaiśca kākaiḥ || 80 ||
children.translated_text: others, helpless, rising up with hands outstretched, are pecked by crows with sharp beaks and talons. || Sl_80 ||
Some, from the touch of worms, and from the falling of swarms of black, flesh-eating flies,

children.text: vṛddhaṃ vraṇantvasahyaṃ bhakṣyamāṇaṃ rudanti cākulā bhūmyām || 81 ||
children.translated_text: with festering, unbearable wounds being devoured, cry out distressed on the ground. || Sl_81 ||

children.text: dahyante 'gnikuṇḍeṣu tena tadānanāni ca bhavanti vivṛtāni /
children.translated_text: They are burned in fire-pits, and therefore their mouths gape open;
they are boiled in iron cauldrons like rice-grains, head downward. || Sl_82 ||

children.text: śvāsāvarodhasamaye pāpaḥ kālaṃkṛte ca narakaṃ prayāti /
children.translated_text: At the moment of the cessation of breath, the sinner, having died, goes to hell;
even one of diamond-nature, hearing of the sufferings of hell a thousandfold, is terrified. || Sl_83 ||

children.text: śrutvā dṛṣṭvā smṛtvā paṭhitvā cāpi citrāṅkanaṃ narakasya /
children.translated_text: Hearing, seeing, remembering, or reading about the depicted images of hell,
even the mere form causes fear — what need be said of experiencing its unbearable fruition? || Sl_84 ||

children.text: yathā samastasukhānāṃ tṛṣṇākṣaya eva sarvottamaṃ sukhamiti /
children.translated_text: Just as the extinction of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is the highest happiness among all happinesses,
so among all sufferings, the suffering of <s>Avīci</s> hell is the most utterly unbearable. || Sl_85 ||

children.text: ihaikasmiṃśca divase, triśataśūlaghātād bhavati ca yad duḥkham /
children.translated_text: The suffering that arises here in one day from being struck by three hundred spears —

children.text: nārakīyaduḥkhasya hi tatrāpnoti samatāṃ na laghukalāṃ cāpi || 86 ||
children.translated_text: does not equal even the slightest fraction of the suffering of hell. || Sl_86 ||
Even while experiencing terrible and extreme sufferings for up to billions of years,
as long as those unwholesome [deeds] are not exhausted, there is no release from life there. || Sl_87 ||
The seeds of unwanted fruits are the evil actions of body, speech, and mind;

children.text: bhavataivaṃ yatanīyaṃ śaktyā yena tadaṇumātraṃ na śiṣyeta || 88 ||
children.translated_text: therefore one should strive with all one's might so that not even an atom of that remains. || Sl_88 ||

children.text: tiryagyoniṣu nānā duḥkhāni bhavanti ca badhabandhanādīni /
children.translated_text: In the animal realm there are various sufferings — slaughter, bondage, and the like;
they devour one another — those who have abandoned the wholesome <s>karma</s> that is the root of peace. || Sl_89 ||
Some living beings are killed for their pearls, wool, bones, flesh, and skin;

children.text: yojyante khalu vivaśā anye padamuṣṭikaśāṅkuśaiḥ paśavaśca || 90 ||
children.translated_text: others, helpless, are controlled by kicks, fists, whips, and goads. || Sl_90 ||

children.text: pretayonau na kṣayaṃ yātīṣṭālābhajanitā duḥkhadhārā ca /
children.translated_text: In the <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) realm, the stream of suffering born from not obtaining what is desired does not diminish;
they obtain unbearable suffering born from cold, heat, hunger, thirst, exhaustion, and fear. || Sl_91 ||
The mouths of some are like the eye of a needle, but their bellies are vast as a mountain;

children.text: tacca pīḍitaṃ kṣudhayā kṣiptamaśuci vastu na pratikārakṣamam || 92 ||
children.translated_text: tormented by hunger, they are unable to consume even a discarded impure morsel. || Sl_92 ||
Some <s>pretas</s> are naked, with skin and bones like the top of a withered palm tree;
at night, from those who vomit fire from their mouths, hot sand falls into their mouths as food. || Sl_93 ||

children.text: nimnakoṭikaiḥ kaiścit pūyaraktādyaśucīni na ca labhyante /
children.translated_text: Some of low station cannot obtain even impure things like pus and blood;
climbing on top of one another, they eat the mucus and saliva dripping from the throats of others. || Sl_94 ||

children.text: candro grīṣme taptaḥ śaitye śīto bhānuśca hyetebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For them the moon is hot in summer and the sun is cold in winter;

children.text: teṣāṃ dṛṣṭi pātācca niṣphalāstaravo nadyaśca śuṣyante || 95 ||
children.translated_text: from their mere glance, trees become fruitless and rivers dry up. || Sl_95 ||
Constantly sharing in suffering, firmly bound by the noose of evil <s>karma</s>,

children.text: na ca mriyante kecit pañca vā daśa sahasravarṣāṇi sattvāḥ || 96 ||
children.translated_text: some beings do not die for five or ten thousand years. || Sl_96 ||
That which the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) experience—the manifold taste of various sufferings—
the delight therein through miserliness—jealousy is ignoble; thus the <s>Buddha</s> declared.
Even the excessive happiness in heaven is followed by still greater suffering from the fall therefrom, certainly;

children.text: evaṃ vicintya tajjñaiḥ kṣaratsukhāya na tṛṣṇā kāryā svarge || 98 ||
children.translated_text: having reflected thus, the wise should not crave for the fleeting happiness of heaven.

children.text: vaivarṇyaṃ dehasya svāsane na ratirmlāyate 'pi mālā ca /
children.translated_text: The body's complexion fades, one finds no pleasure in one's seat, the garlands wither,
a foul smell arises from the garments, and an unprecedented sweat issues forth from the body.
These indeed are the five signs of death that appear in the gods dwelling in heaven,
similar to the signs of death among humans on earth.
If, upon falling from the gods, not even an atom of wholesome merit remains,
then helplessly one must dwell in one of the realms—animal, <s>preta</s>, or hell.
Mental suffering arises in the <s>Asuras</s> too through jealousy of the splendor of the gods,

children.text: na kurvanti dhīmanto janmāvaraṇācca te satyadarśanāni || 102 ||
children.translated_text: and the wise among them do not see the truths, due to the obscuration of rebirth.
Thus in this <s>saṃsāra</s>, in the destinies of gods, hells, <s>pretas</s>, and animals,
taking birth is unwholesome; birth therein should be known as full of afflictions.

children.text: jvalite śirasi ca vasane tannivṛttyupāyamupekṣya tvaritameva /
children.translated_text: Even when one's head and clothing are on fire, one should disregard efforts to extinguish them and swiftly
strive for the end of rebirth, for there is no greater purpose than that.
Through <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge)—free from earth, water, fire, wind, the sun and moon—
one should attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>, which is ageless, deathless, imperishable, peaceful, tamed, and immaculate.
Tranquility, vigor, joy, investigation of <s>dharmas</s>, mindfulness, concentration, and equanimity—these seven
are the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (limbs of awakening), the accumulation of wholesome factors for the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: prajñābhāve dhyānaṃ dhyānābhāve 'pi na jāyate sā prajñā /
children.translated_text: Without <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) does not arise; without <s>dhyāna</s>, that <s>prajñā</s> does not arise either;
for one in whom both are present, the ocean of existence becomes like a hoofprint of a cow.
The fourteen indeterminate questions (<s>avyākṛtadharmas</s>) taught by the Kinsman of the Sun (<s>Ādityabandhu</s>)

children.text: loke na cintanīyā yato tairnāpnoti cittameva śāntim || 108 ||
children.translated_text: should not be pondered upon in the world, for through them the mind does not attain peace.

children.text: evaṃ proktaṃ munināvidyayā karma karmaṇā ca vijñānam /
children.translated_text: Thus the sage declared: from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arises <s>karma</s> (action), from <s>karma</s> arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness),

children.text: tasmācca nāmarūpaṃ tataḥ ṣaḍāyatanāni tataḥ sparśā vai || 109 ||
children.translated_text: from that arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), from that the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), from those arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact);

children.text: tata utpannā vittirvedanāśrayeṇa jāyate khalu tṛṣṇā /
children.translated_text: from that arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), and depending on feeling arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving);

children.text: tasyāścopādānaṃ tato bhavo 'pi bhavācca jāyate jātiḥ || 110 ||
children.translated_text: from craving arises <s>upādāna</s> (grasping), from that <s>bhava</s> (becoming), and from becoming arises <s>jāti</s> (birth).
When birth exists, there arise suffering, disease, old age, loss of what is desired, failure to obtain things, fear, and death—
a vast mass of suffering; when birth is prevented, all these are prevented.
Profound, the priceless treasure, the beloved <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) of the <s>Jina</s>'s (Victor's) words—

children.text: samyagimaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa ca paśyati tattvadarśinaṃ buddhameva || 112 ||
children.translated_text: one who rightly sees this truly sees the <s>Buddha</s> himself, the seer of reality.
For the sake of peace, one should cultivate right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right mindfulness,
right concentration, and right effort—these are the noble eightfold path, cultivated with beauty.

children.text: jātiriyaṃ duḥkhameva tṛṣṇā ca tasya samudayo mahān jñeyaḥ /
children.translated_text: This birth is indeed suffering itself, and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is to be known as its great cause of origination;
cessation is <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and this eightfold path is for its attainment.
Thus, effort should always be made for the penetration of the four noble truths;

children.text: kroḍe śriyaśca yeṣāṃ gṛhasthāstaranti kleśanadīṃ jñānāt || 115 ||
children.translated_text: even householders in whose laps prosperity dwells cross the river of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) through knowledge.
Those who have seen the noble truths do not manifest like a sprout from the earth;

children.text: nāvataranti ca gaganāt te 'pi pṛthagjanāḥ kleśavaśā hi pūrvam || 116 ||
children.translated_text: nor do they descend from the sky—they too were formerly ordinary beings under the sway of afflictions.

children.text: cittaṃ hi dharmamūlaṃ bhagavatoktamatastadapi sādhu damayecca /
children.translated_text: The mind is the root of <s>Dharma</s>—thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> declared; therefore, tame it well.

children.text: bho nirbhaya, kiṃ bahunā kathanena yato 'yameva hitopadeśaḥ || 117 ||
children.translated_text: O Fearless One, what use is much elaboration? For this alone is the beneficial counsel.
What has been taught by me is difficult to accomplish even by monks with great effort;

children.text: caryāguṇān sevasva śikṣāmācara jīvanaṃ ca kuru sārtham || 118 ||
children.translated_text: cultivate the virtues of practice, carry out the training, and make your life meaningful.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ kuśalāni tu sarvārthamanumodya svacaryātrayīṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having rejoiced in the wholesome deeds of all beings for the sake of all purposes, and [dedicating] your own threefold conduct,
dedicate them toward Buddhahood; then, through this heap of merit, may you—
having mastered in immeasurable births the states of gods, humans, and yogins—
help the suffering, friendless beings through the practices of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Having taken your final birth, having abandoned disease, old age, desire, and hatred,
like <s>Bhagavān Amitābha</s>, become a lord of the world with immeasurable life, in a <s>Buddha</s>-field.
Having spread throughout the earth, sky, and heaven the stainless renown born of wisdom, moral conduct, and generosity,

children.text: loke prasārya śamayan narān yuvatisukharatadevāṃśca bhūmau || 122 ||
children.translated_text: pacifying in this world humans and gods delighting in the pleasures of youth, upon the earth,
for beings afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (defilements)—attain the station called '<s>Jinendra</s>' (Lord of Victors), which destroys birth, fear, and death,
which is supramundane, undefiled, and bears the very name of peace, fearlessness, and imperishability.

body.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Suhṛllekha</s> (Letter to a Friend).
